chapter: Arranging craft, ownership and the business
title: Where arranging ideas come from
summary: The song itself provides the ideas; he plays it through and something in the melody triggers an intro or shout chorus.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So a while back I watched, it was a pretty good documentary on Quincy Jones. But I was disappointed that no one asked him where do your arranging ideas come from. It was mostly just people saying, you know, how great he was and his whole resume, which is incredible. So my question to you is, can you tell me where your arranging ideas, how do they occur to you?

The song does it. You take the song that you’re arranging and that tells you everything. It gives you everything you need. It really does. You know you can change — rhythmically or harmonically you’ve got all the material to work with. And every now — well maybe it’s just the talent, but I’ll go through, first of all I play through the song and listen to it, and then something will spring out, like oh here’s a good introduction or here’s a good shout chorus or you know, something in that melody, because that’s what you’re working with, something in that melody will trigger something and then the brain starts taking over. Mancini was that way too. He said that the melody is the thing. Everything is unimportant but it’s the melody that we have to support. And he was a smart guy.
